findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "rpc" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_data_status · Private data: register_autonomous_agent · Public sink: submit_agent_trade_idea · Destructive: run_quant_simulation, analyze_stock_ai.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_data_status · Private data: register_autonomous_agent · Public sink: submit_agent_trade_idea · Destructive: run_quant_simulation, analyze_stock_ai

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "register_autonomous_agent" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Self-register an autonomous AI agent to receive a permanent API key (sb_live_*) and 100 free platform trial credits. (Free - No Auth Required)." → after: "Self-register an autonomous AI agent to receive a permanent API key (sb_live_*). (Free - No Auth Required)."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
